enonce_intro_markdown:
The probability density function, $f$, of a random variable $X$ is given by

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{12}(2x + 1), & 0 \le x \le 3, \\ 0, & \text{elsewhere.} \end{cases}$$

Calculate

questions.corrige_markdown:
(Check that $f$ is a p.d.f.: $\displaystyle\int_0^3 \frac{2x+1}{12}\,dx = \frac{1}{12}\left[x^2 + x\right]_0^3 = \frac{12}{12} = 1$.)

$$E(X) = \int_0^3 x f(x)\,dx = \frac{1}{12}\int_0^3 (2x^2 + x)\,dx = \frac{1}{12}\left[\frac{2x^3}{3} + \frac{x^2}{2}\right]_0^3 = \frac{1}{12}\left(18 + \frac{9}{2}\right) = \frac{22.5}{12}$$

**$E(X) = \dfrac{15}{8} = 1.875$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) the upper quartile of $X$, giving the answer to three decimal places.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The upper quartile $q$ satisfies $P(X \le q) = 0.75$. For $0 \le x \le 3$ the cumulative distribution function is

$$F(x) = \int_0^x \frac{2t + 1}{12}\,dt = \frac{x^2 + x}{12}$$

$$\frac{q^2 + q}{12} = \frac{3}{4} \;\Rightarrow\; q^2 + q - 9 = 0 \;\Rightarrow\; q = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{37}}{2}$$

The root must lie in $[0, 3]$, so $q = \dfrac{-1 + \sqrt{37}}{2} = 2.5413\ldots$ (the other root is negative). Check: $F(2.5414) = \dfrac{6.4585 + 2.5414}{12} = 0.75$.

**Upper quartile $= 2.541$ (3 d.p.).**
